# Trellis

Operation starts default to canonical routing. Explicit targeted starts persist
deployment, invocation ULID, and frozen input before the first send and never
fall back to another deployment. They cannot recover an unknown owner after an
uncertain canonical start. See the TypeScript and Rust guides for typed APIs.
Both live testkits support ordinary distinct users, explicit capability grants,
and independent logins to one registered app without borrowing administrator
identity or automatically restoring revoked grants.

Rust and Node replicas use one deployment-scoped Operation storage codec. This
pre-release persistence cutover does not migrate earlier records: retain existing
installations unchanged and use fresh development/test state. Unsupported records
fail visibly; the runtime never deletes or recreates them as empty state.

Generated SDKs are disposable build artifacts, not maintained source. Commit native
IDL, manifests, and dependency locks; run `trellis install` before compiling
project-local consumers. Trellis-owned Rust bindings build in Cargo `OUT_DIR`.

Console and the isolated OAuth listener require HTTPS outside explicit loopback
development. The HTTP insecure-origin allowlist does not relax that requirement.

Fresh startup creates the protected administrator before provider admission.
Username defaults to `admin`; omitting an initial password returns `adminAccountUrl`,
a one-time password-setup link on the isolated OAuth origin (five-minute expiry).
Use startup flags `--admin-username`, `--admin-password`, or
`--admin-password-stdin`, or `trellis init admin --config <path>` with
`--username`, `--password`, or `--password-stdin`. Until password setup, each startup
prints a fresh setup link and invalidates prior links. After setup, restart preserves
credentials and prints no link. `--reset-admin` explicitly issues a replacement
reset link; ordinary RPCs cannot reset the protected administrator.

Service Jobs reconstruct retained lifecycle history through the deployment-scoped
runtime `Jobs.History` route automatically. Use generated service job handles;
ordinary service identities cannot read the shared JOBS stream directly.
Detaching resources retains data. Explicit administrative deletion removes only
the selected detached allocation; shared streams and other queues remain intact.
Missing previously materialized durable resources fail closed; restart or
provisioning retries do not create empty replacements. Restore coherent durable
state rather than resetting Job consumers, keyed ownership, or Operation storage.
Runtime Jobs/Events resource evidence is read from Auth through authenticated
`ResourceBindings.Query`, with separate kind-scoped read capabilities. Split roles
do not read another role's SQLite database; application services continue using
generated resource handles rather than this runtime-internal evidence API.
Identical deployment Apply retains current ready resource evidence. Changed or
unmaterialized resources remain unavailable until reconciled; Apply does not
promote stale materialization evidence.

Operator CLI: `trellis clients list|get|put|disable|delete` manages public OAuth
registrations, including exact loopback browser redirects.
Auth client flows are fixed on every Put: browser callbacks enable Authorization
Code + refresh; native without callbacks enables Device Code + refresh; native
with callbacks enables both + refresh. Adding/removing native callbacks updates
the supported flows. Kind is immutable; use a new client ID to switch kind.
Native HTTP loopback callbacks need no development flag; browser loopback does.
`put` reads generated AuthOAuthClientPutRequest JSON; mutations are revision-fenced. `trellis apis
list|get|review|accept|force-replace` uses generated Auth request JSON and reviewed
package evidence. Force replacement requires apis.forceReplace and explicit
breakage/consent acknowledgements. Console exposes OAuth clients and API catalog.

Durable event consumers verify original broker publication time. DLQ/replay retains
that provenance in the existing journal and resolves original bytes and timestamp
through authenticated, resource-scoped Events inspection, including after source
expiry. Publisher headers and replay publication time never replace it.

Cold OAuth resume verifies signed issuer successors from the retained pin using
GET /.well-known/trellis/issuer-chain at the selected OAuth origin and persists
successor trust before spending a refresh token. Unavailable or invalid chains
leave it unspent. A successfully returned new token survives later issuer
verification failure, but its admission remains unusable until authenticated.
Never retry an ambiguously spent predecessor.
Node-native and browser transport recovery reuse admission only while shared verification
accepts its lifetime and current pinned trust. Transport loss alone does not
spend refresh custody. Renewal checks the selected HTTP origin before spending
the token; an ambiguous token POST still requires explicit recovery. Preparation
retries never retransmit application requests or clear known revocations.

Native providers finish accepted RPCs across ordinary authority promotion by
reacquiring a coherent current signing snapshot within one configured deadline.
Handlers are not redispatched; provider, issuer, expiry and revocation checks remain mandatory.
Accepted finite responses may outlive the opening caller context, but not their
request deadline. Current provider verification, known revocation, cancellation
and logical shutdown remain enforced; expired evidence cannot start new work.
Store object deletion and replacement clean up chunks only in the admitted
identity's allocated Object Store streams, including Operation staging. This
does not authorize KV purge, stream destruction, or cross-owner Store access.

Account actions use generated Auth RPCs and the isolated OAuth portal.
PasswordReset.Create returns a five-minute, one-use token for `/account/reset`;
completion checks Origin/CSRF, credential CAS, and the requester's original active
session/current accepted `principals.manage`, then revokes login/grant families.
Bootstrap administrators use local recovery. IdentityLink.Create returns a
five-minute portal URL requiring the exact initiating user and fresh verified
OIDC with nonce/PKCE. Provider changes and cross-user identity collisions fail;
creation replay never renews or revives an action.

Identity-link approval remains a protected same-origin POST. Its no-store
continuation page shows a navigation link to a 60-second, one-use GET handoff
bound to the exact portal session, provider and account. Top-level navigation
reaches the verified IdP without relaxing form-action 'self' or leaking the
handoff in referrers. Direct, expired and replayed handoffs fail.

Provisioned services/devices publish native Health.Heartbeat events automatically
with ordinary SessionEvent signatures and the runtime-only selfReport capability.
Users/apps cannot obtain that publishing right. The collector verifies catalog
authority, broker chronology, retirement cutoff and signed native identity;
payload claims never establish deployment, instance or participant digest.
Initial publication is asynchronous and does not gate service connection.

Fresh administrator initialization explicitly grants only the current accepted
Trellis-owned Auth/Core/State/Health/Jobs/Events capabilities, atomically with
finite platform privileges and Console/CLI registration. Replay does not grant
future capabilities or rewrite clients; domain APIs remain explicitly granted.
App connections still require selection, consent, and client privilege eligibility.

OAuth authority/admission renewal is bounded by the original verified refresh
family's absolute deadline and revocation state, never another family's lifetime.
Live same-key Admission.Renew returns short signed admission without rotating
refresh tokens; provisioned admission still needs the client's identity signature.

Trellis provides authenticated, contract-defined communication and runtime
resources for TypeScript and Rust participants. Native IDL generates each
participant's typed API. Connected calls run over NATS; the libraries own
bootstrap, proofs, authorization, and connection lifecycle.

## Scope

Completed device activation rechecks authenticate the retained challenge instead
of opening another review; local completion is not authorization. Generated Rust
device State Watch support needs no built-in API package dependency.

App State uses native-IDL projected registration with explicit CAS. Rust generated
accessors are async and return `(handle, registration)`; TypeScript handles register
before use and expose `register(expectedRevision, idempotencyKey)`. Start at "0";
identical registration returns its revision, changes require explicit current
revision, and conflicts never trigger blind retry. Typed `watch()` uses certified
Live initial/update snapshots and in-memory migrations. Unwritten/deleted snapshots
are None/undefined. Close observations; transport/authorization loss does not silently
reopen them. See the language guides for ownership and terminal-outcome APIs.

Own-context bootstrap signs the exact physical socket's broker `attachmentId`
and verifies its echoed signed registry ID; overlapping sockets never select
the newest attachment as a fallback.

Already admitted connections resolve public verification metadata through the
read-only `trellis.auth.metadata.get` bootstrap, not administrative Authority.Status.
SDKs verify issuer signatures, pinned rotation trust, retained nonce/routing and
freshness; missing/unavailable responses never clear revocation or grant authority.

Request verification checks caller grants against the caller's exact signed
catalog reference, independently of the provider's pinned implementation and
certificate. Compatible accepted revisions within one API generation need not
match; neither catalog grants additional rights to the other party.

This unreleased Revision 7 branch implements authoritative Auth capability
evaluation, reviewed catalog acceptance, logical authorization sessions, signed
verification material, and durable retirement effects. OAuth/Callout admission
and SDK/provider transports use this model; do not adapt applications to
the former browser-bind or GrantBinding protocols. Use matching runtime,
SDK, and generated package versions.

Revision 7's OAuth components use a separate, required login/consent portal
from Console. Their origins must differ; hostnames need not differ, but sharing
a hostname emits a security warning because cookies are not port-scoped. TLS
is required outside explicitly configured loopback development. Installation
identity and the independently provisioned OAuth storage key survive restarts
and issuer rotation. Admin `Issuers.Rotate` durably creates successor custody
and a signed trust-chain link; back up the Auth database's sibling
`<database-stem>.issuer-keys` directory (`platform.issuer-keys` by default)
with the Auth database. Missing committed keys stop startup.
Browser credential custody uses nonextractable keys and
cross-tab refresh ownership; Rust native custody uses owner-only files and a
cross-process family lock. Node custody is process-local unless explicitly supplied
by the application.

Node native applications use `@oatscenter/trellis/native` for Device Code OAuth,
process-local memory custody, and generated native callers. Retain an explicit
MemoryNativeOAuthCustody object for reconnects in one process. Remembered login
across process restarts requires an application-owned NativeOAuthCustody provider;
there is no built-in persistent Node backend or SQLite requirement. Persistent
providers must exclusively own the family and durably commit spent-token markers,
successors, and authenticated trust before their operations resolve. This entrypoint is
Node/npm-only; browser applications retain IndexedDB and Web Locks. Successful
connection transfers credential ownership to the connection until it closes.
Await native connection.close() before reacquiring: asynchronous lease release
is joined exactly once and release failures remain observable.
Discovery cannot replace a retained issuer pin; only an authenticated rotation
chain can advance it. Lost refresh responses require recovery, not token replay.
Live authority requires a verified initial revocation snapshot and ongoing
coverage; old watchers cannot restore or clear replacement coverage.
TypeScript requests wait for missing verified authority within their original
deadline and cancellation, rather than treating it as optional-capability denial;
current denials remain enforced and requests are never replayed.
Rust and TypeScript preserve healthy predecessor coverage during mirror rollover.
Replacement application IO stays fenced until authenticated replay and checked
handover; actual coverage loss stays unavailable until private recovery, without
clearing revocations or retransmitting application requests.

Provisioned native connections use explicit broker endpoints and pinned runtime
trust, never caller-selected deployments in CONNECT. The Rust SDK retains native
OAuth custody and renews admission with the same runtime key; uncertain refresh
requires recovery rather than replaying a spent token.

Explicitly registered loopback development clients may be eligible for
platform privileges only when authorized registration configures eligibility,
the user holds the privileges, and the user explicitly delegates them. Localhost
and development mode grant no trust; CIMD clients remain ineligible.

Finite administrative privileges are explicit OAuth requests, not native IDL
selections or generated contract authority. Browser connections use
`auth.platformPrivileges: { required, optional }`; normal client eligibility,
user authority, and consent checks apply, including to optional requests.

Explicit one-off consent overrides older remembered choices without changing
them. Reused choices retain their expiry; later shared withdrawals still retire
affected sessions. A shortened effective authorization deadline is a reduction
unless another entitlement path preserves the outstanding authority.
Consent approval binds the current server-owned presentation and the selected
optional capabilities; stale forms require a fresh presentation. Signed session
authority has a shared 64 KiB issuer, verification, and parsing budget.
Provisional CIMD client intake shares a 128-client/16 MiB budget and a five-minute
lifetime; live decisions and approved refresh lifecycles are retained. Exhaustion
returns `temporarily_unavailable`, not administrative registration or authority.
Deadlines on newly gained rights bound new contexts, not older narrower contexts
or the logical-session root.

Revision 7's breaking routing cutover uses canonical generated API/action
subjects for RPC, Operation starts, and Live openings. Providers sharing a
logical API share request queues and must be suitable alternatives; identical
IDL does not make independent databases or physical devices interchangeable.
Signed provider identity, generation/action checks, and service-owned resources
remain separate from caller capabilities. Established Live/Transfer traffic
and existing Operation controls retain owner-directed routing. There is no
persisted caller-to-deployment selection or automatic retry of potentially
executed requests. This decision is still being integrated on this branch.

Provisioned services/devices prove possession of their identity key and a fresh
runtime/session key for the configured installation/account. Auth derives their
deployment, instance, participant, and implementation authority from current
provisioning records; clients never assert those bindings during CONNECT.
Provisioning still supplies broker endpoints and pinned installation/issuer trust.
Immediate ServiceInstances.Provision and Devices.Provision require identityPublicKey
from a client-owned Ed25519 key. Trellis never stores or returns its private seed.
Missing identityPublicKey returns identity_public_key_required without provisioning
or consuming the idempotency key. provisioningSecret is null; activation-token
provisioning is not implemented. CONNECT proves possession of the registered key.
ServiceInstances.Provision awaits the ordinary native resource producer before
success (empty declarations and KV supported; other declarations fail explicitly).
Retry the same request after broker failure; retained allocations are never destroyed.

Auth.Resources.List/Get include all allocation states, including detached, with
digest resourceId, ownerKind (user/deployment), ownerId, and explicit state.
Declaration omission and deployment Remove detach and retain resource data;
Disable preserves resource bindings but revokes sessions and denies admission.
Enable reuses retained bindings without reapplying the contract or recreating storage;
there is no automatic resource deletion. Compatible re-add reuses retained data.
Explicit admin Resources.Remove permanently deletes only the selected detached
owned KV at expectedRevision after checking its physical ownership marker. Retry
the same manual request after broker failure; startup never resumes deletion.
Removal execution is exclusively claimed and incarnation-fenced. Recreating a
deleted logical resource uses a fresh allocation and physical bucket, so delayed
deletion cannot touch replacement data; compatible reattachment keeps the original.
KV history/TTL reductions that could lose retained data are rejected.

Auth Connections.Opened/Closed/Kicked publish generated AuthSecurityEvent values
through the admitted Auth provider. Event IDs and occurrence times survive durable
outbox retries; consumers should identify attachments by attachmentId and logical
authority by authorizationSessionId, not retired connection/session-key fields.
An expired delivery claim alone does not stop Auth: stale workers cannot
acknowledge or reschedule the intent, which remains recoverable by its next owner.

This guidance covers Trellis interfaces, not application engineering policy.
Services choose their configuration and validation libraries, databases, domain
models, dependency injection, project layout, and development tools. Examples
choose a concrete stack to demonstrate Trellis, not to require that stack.

Use documentation from the same Trellis release or source revision as the
installed libraries and CLI. For a local checkout, these files live under
`docs/static/`. The links below address the main branch and may be newer than an
installed release.

## Start Here

- [Consumer guide](llms-full.txt): project files, generation, participants,
  communication, authorization, resources, and testing.
- [TypeScript](llms-typescript.txt): service connection, generated handlers,
  events, operations, and transactional outbox integration.
- [Rust](llms-rust.txt): generated Cargo crates, connection options, typed
  callers, providers, resources, lifecycle, and opt-in SQL event stores.
- [Svelte](llms-svelte.txt): browser authentication and the Svelte integration.
- Human service walkthrough: `/guides/write-a-service`.
- Human IDL authoring guide: `/guides/authoring-contracts`.
- Human testing walkthrough: `/guides/testing-trellis-services`.
- Public API reference: `/api` on the docs site. Generated participant source
  defines the exact names available for a project's declared actions.

## Essential Workflow

Services and devices are deployable principals. Apps and agents author application
request descriptors, not installable principals. Select whole capabilities in
native IDL: `required capability read;` is required and `capability export;` is
optional. Generated callers expose the selected actions; inspect capability
availability before using an optional capability. API authors supply positive
`consent_revision` values; Auth owns acceptance and introduction counters.

Administrative Auth RPCs require ordinary capability/action authorization plus
the applicable finite platform privilege. Selecting an administrative capability
does not confer that privilege. Own-authority/session maintenance uses fixed
session rights rather than ordinary capability requests.

Provider-owned event publication requires the exact issuer-verified publish
action in the certificate bound to the signed native authority and its native
deployment/instance/implementation, API generation, and action revision—not
consumer capabilities. Certificates never grant RPC calls or event consumption.
Delegated publication remains whole-capability authorized.

Historical event verification uses the signed event time and trusted original
JetStream publication time/stream sequence, never the consumer's read time.
Both timestamps must precede ordinary session revocation and authority
expiry; certified publication also requires both times within its certificate's
validity window. Current permission to read is a separate authorization check.
Ordinary certificate expiry or issuer retirement does not invalidate authentic
retained publications, including cold replay. Compromised issuers remain unusable.

1. Author the `.trellis` files explicitly listed by `[sources]`.
2. Set `[package]`, `[dependencies]`, and language outputs in `trellis.toml`;
   run `trellis update` to resolve changes into `trellis.lock`. A durable
   `consumer` needs a direct `trellis` package dependency containing
   `trellis.events@v1`; choose its version explicitly.
3. Run `trellis install` to reproduce locked dependencies and `trellis generate`
   after IDL edits. `trellis generate --watch` supports the edit loop.
4. Depend on the one ordinary generated package for your language. Import its
   `apis`, `participants`, and `apps` namespaces, not separate API or participant
   packages.
5. Connect through that participant's supported runtime API. Use generated calls
   and resolved resource handles; do not reconstruct Trellis transport metadata.

Commit authored IDL, `trellis.toml`, and `trellis.lock`, not generated
implementations. Run `trellis install` before local consumers build, and package
generated code when distributing consumers. Configure `[generate.rust].output`
and/or `[generate.typescript].output`. Explicit targets are authoritative;
without them, detection uses root Cargo or npm manifests. With neither explicit
targets nor markers, no language package is emitted. Package version equals the
source package version. TypeScript packages contain executable ESM JavaScript
and declarations; Rust packages are ordinary path-dependency crates. Both use
published runtime dependencies matching the CLI. No project-local installation
tree, runtime-path configuration, or consumer transpilation step is required.
Use exact declared action names, not suffixes or invented qualifiers. Failed
compilation, rendering, or formatting retains the last successful generated
outputs; colliding participant output paths are errors.

Trellis Operations are durable, restartable, at-least-once caller-visible
workflows. New starts use canonical API subjects. Complete serialized references
require `deploymentId`, checked against certified signed acceptance; the SDK
routes existing controls and observations to that deployment, not an instance.
Restore complete references, never ID-only handles. Invocation deduplication is
deployment-scoped: never automatically retry an uncertain canonical start or
claim cross-deployment idempotency. References are routing metadata, not authority.
RPC cancellation stops the caller's wait, not work already accepted by the
service. TypeScript `RequestOpts.signal` reports `trellis.request.cancelled`
even after publication; deadline expiry reports `trellis.request.timeout`.
Neither undoes accepted work. Use Operation cancellation for business work.

Controls remain bound to the creator principal and participant across
reconnects, and terminal states are immutable. An Operation observer is a
separate live session from the durable executor: a watcher reconciles the
current authoritative snapshot once its transport is ready, then delivers typed
transient updates and terminal state. Get and initial watcher snapshots expose
persisted state, not speculative handler state; a committed write may be visible
after its ACK is lost. Transient updates are ordered and never
silently dropped, while not-yet-delivered nonterminal snapshots may be
conflated. Opening or closing a watcher never starts, cancels, or completes the
durable work, and a transport interruption surfaces as an observation error
rather than an invented terminal business state. Jobs are service-private; keyed
capacity waits do not consume attempts. Service operation registrations expose
local owner-fenced `control(id)` and owner-routed `reconcile(id)`, which
re-enters the handler with persisted input, caller, and progress. A cancellation
request stays nonterminal while the owner renews its lease and joins handler
cleanup; only then is `Cancelled` persisted. Stalled cleanup has no forced
terminal timeout, and external side effects may overlap across owner loss.
Cancellation-first admission requires both Invoke and Cancel authority and the
same caller-chosen invocation ID and input on every retry. It atomically records
non-clearable cancellation intent; the handler must perform already-aborted
cleanup before business work. Errors or explicit deferral leave cleanup pending.
Job deadlines are creation-relative; retry defaults to five ordinary attempts
delayed by 5s, 30s, 2m, and 10m. Broker redelivery is unlimited so execution
owners can finish cleanup before Expired or Dead. Already-cancelled handlers
must reconcile earlier side effects; cleanup errors preserve redelivery.
Never-started expiration confirms terminal publication before releasing
recovered key slots, without running handlers; terminal redelivery reconciles
any remaining slot before acknowledgement. Ordinary queues use Block. At the
coordinator boundary, fail-stale takeover preserves cleanup for the displaced
job's recovered owner under a fresh fence; only that owner settles Stale.
Ignored stale completions are nonterminal diagnostics and retain redelivery
until cleanup settles. A never-started displaced reservation settles Pending to
Stale without handler execution. Lifecycle publication awaits JetStream
acknowledgement; typed live updates remain transient. Execution state and
attempts follow accepted lifecycle transitions in broker stream-sequence order.
Created initializes but cannot reopen a job. Diagnostics cannot override
settlement or attempts. A valid Retried opens a new run without deleting
history. Old-run deliveries are identified by their original lifecycle sequence
and acknowledged without touching newer-run coordination. Deferred work rereads
lifecycle state before acquisition. Jobs Summary is independent of Query pages.
Capability approval is not an exact grant. Resource commitments are approvals;
desired capacities are hints, while observed bindings are the usable limits.
Trellis neither adopts nor destroys foreign-owned physical resources. Removal
detaches access without deleting new-version data, allowing compatible approved
reattachment. Store and file metadata listing uses opaque, query-bound keyset
cursors with a default limit of 100 and maximum of 500. An administrator
installs the immutable participant revision and writes a participant-scoped
`GrantBinding`; deployment apply provisions exact resource evidence.
Store streaming uses demand-driven, byte-capped reads and verifies chunk order,
size, and SHA-256 before successful EOF; partial output is not a verified object.
Backend consumer expiry permits exact-cursor continuation on the pinned
connection, not transport reconnection. Cleanup retains the generation lease.
Whole-buffer helpers retain the entire object; bounded source buffering is not a
whole-process memory guarantee. Native ObjectStore links are unsupported.
Services/devices bootstrap with identity and proof inputs only, while browsers
bind a user login and then refresh. Device enrollment consumes a one-use
administrator-issued secret with durable and ephemeral possession proofs;
Devices.Reviews.Get/Decide require its confirmation code and current revision.
A declared native companion uses ordinary explicit OAuth consent through its
current accepted declaration; removing it rejects new/pending consent without
revoking existing independently consented grants. Association removal by its
user or a currently delegated principals.manage administrator revokes only the
associated grant and families. The dedicated OAuth client is the
deployment-scoped client trellis.device.<deploymentId>.companion. Registration
grants no user authority. Its verified user caller associates the grant through
DeviceCompanions.Attach; parent credentials cannot substitute. Removing the
association revokes that exact grant/families, not other grants or the user login.
Parent and child maintain separate connections and revocation. Authorization
contexts, route JWTs, transports, grants, and issuer
keys remain process-memory-only. Requests/events carry context digest, matching
redundant `session-key`, and a message-specific proof.

Browser sign-in carries a reusable signed intent; a bounded authentication
transaction starts only when authentication begins, not when the portal renders.
Only one outstanding attempt can claim an intent; concurrent starts cannot
replace it. Persist the pending portal binding before the start request and
reuse it after response loss or reload: same-binding retries recover the active
transaction; another binding conflicts. Detached progress requires the initiating
key's fresh proof, while
public portal rendering exposes no transaction discovery. Denied, expired, or
consumed attempts can restart from the same intent. Invalid login requires
authentication; valid-login authorization denial surfaces its machine code
without automatically sending the user through another login.

Events use API-qualified subjects and base64url parameter tokens; their signed
descriptor binds the exact API, dotted event name, and parameter count. Durable
delivery acknowledges success only after the handler succeeds; exhausted deliveries
are not acknowledged. Events captures broker max-deliveries advisories into the
per-Consumer DLQ. Consumer ownership does not grant Replay/Dismiss authority. Manual
replay uses the same handler and a fresh delivery budget without rewinding the
original Consumer, and successful replay is durably resolved before
acknowledgement. Live observations and Operation watchers are authorized live
sessions negotiated with bounded opening requests; the provider signs its offer
and frames, control responses bind the session ID, logical command sequence, and
command hash, and continued authority is rechecked from retained context rather
than by a network lookup per frame. Sessions have protocol liveness and credit
bounds, not a total age or message cap; an explicit close returns a receipt
whose remote-cleanup state is complete, incomplete, or unconfirmed, and
reconnect is an explicit new open rather than a silent reopen.

Live uses `trellis.live.v1` even for application APIs such as `documents@v2`.
Generated canonical opening subjects are
`live.v1.route.<b64(full_api_id)>.<action>`, with unpadded base64url identity
tokens. The application's major belongs to that full API identity, not to the
Live protocol version. Use generated client/provider facades; dotted action
names never imply a deployment selection or another Live protocol.

Transfer v1 uses bounded, windowed raw-byte streaming over NATS, with storage
protocols and credentials hidden behind runtime store handles. Use generated
upload Operations and download helpers, not raw subjects. Network credit is not
durability: upload success follows verified backend and durable Operation commit.
TypeScript download callers use `decodeTransferGrant(response.transfer)` from
`@oatscenter/trellis` and check its direction before `client.transfer(grant)`.
This Rust/WASM decoder checks wire structure, not authorization; the transfer
runtime verifies provider identity and session authority before bytes move.

`Auth.Users.List/Get` require selected and consented `usersRead` and return
active directory profiles, including immutable `principalId`, names, available
email and photos. Ordinary profiles omit `account`. Delegated and currently
eligible `principals.manage` also exposes account lifecycle/revision, username
and password status and permits inactive-user lookup and username search.
`Users.Resolve` with `accountRead` is self-only and includes the caller's account.
Names and email are not unique identity keys or application authorization.

Durable transfer progress is monotonic and may be coalesced; interrupted uploads
restart from byte zero.
An upload transport error is not proof that durable commit failed. Resume its
Operation before retrying. TypeScript's connection timeout bounds transfer
activation and each cancellation exchange, not the streaming body lifetime.

Consumer AGENTS templates are available under `templates/`. They describe the
Trellis boundary; application policies belong in the consumer repository.

For live Rust tests, `trellis-testkit` links the real production runtime and
manages a real NATS child without requiring the CLI/server executables. Its bare
builder defaults to the verified pinned broker download; a prebuilt broker can
be selected with `TRELLIS_TEST_NATS_BIN` or `NatsSource`. Only the verified NATS
executable/archive cache is shared (`TRELLIS_CACHE_DIR` or the platform cache),
allowing offline reuse; credentials and runtime state remain private. The
TypeScript testkit
acquires exact-version SHA-256-pinned production CLI/server archives (currently Linux x86-64 only)
automatically; no installed Trellis executables or nsc are required. Production
commands generate configuration and own managed NATS. Graceful TypeScript host
shutdown has a bounded fallback that reclaims the isolated host/broker process
group. Registry-distributed Rust implementation crates are not supported
service-author APIs.
Historical issuer keys are resolved through the existing issuer-signed metadata
exchange, authenticated by the active pinned issuer or its forward-verified
successor. Historical keys never advance live trust; compromised keys remain
unusable. A retired catalog signer does not invalidate an immutable catalog
referenced by current signed authority.

Rejected cross-user Device Code reauthorization preserves existing credentials.
Already-open browser tabs refresh discovery from retained trust before spending
refresh tokens. Native renewal uses the current maintenance attachment through
verified authority promotion, including after transport replacement.

Operations use the canonical `<API identity>@v<major>:operation:<action>` identity
across SDKs, storage and complete references; generated aliases are not durable
identities. Canonical starts honor that API major, while owner-directed controls
retain the fixed `operation.v1` transport family. Implementation-only providers
can forward their own updates without receiving caller Observe authority.

OIDC claim refresh is scoped to the selected provider and upstream subject; a
second linked identity cannot add or remove another identity's mapped roles.

Configured implied consent applies only to registered browser bindings. Native
and Device Code clients require explicit user approval even when registered.
